title: Adaptive spend curtains: SKU-aware spillover arbiter with graceful model ladder
creator: Morgan Reyes
description: Background: We need a routing controller that enforces per-tenant budget curtains while preferring SKU families (A100/T4/H100) and gracefully spilling traffic across regions and model variants when budgets or spot capacity are exhausted. Current router focuses on cost bands but lacks a soft-commit mechanism that guarantees SLO-first behavior while keeping spend under caps. Goal: implement an 'Adaptive Spend Curtains' arbiter that applies progressive throttles and staged model degradation (scale-down quantized variants -> lower-capacity GPU -> fallback model variant) with SKU-aware affinity and predictive spot-eviction hedging.
design_notes: Controller model: per-tenant sliding spend window + headroom buffer (configurable), uses probabilistic hedging when spot eviction risk > threshold
Affinity: annotate capacity pool SKUs with accelerator_fingerprint; prefer families that match tenant performance profile, degrade to compatible SKUs when constrained

Spillover ladder: 1) full-res model on preferred SKU, 2) quantized variant on same SKU, 3) same model on lower-class SKU, 4) compatible smaller model variant, 5) queued/slow-path with cached-prefix responses
Budget curtains: soft caps trigger progressive throttles and routing to cheaper SKUs; hard caps enforce reject/queue and alerting
Routing decision factors: tenant SLO, budget burn rate, spot eviction forecast, regional latency delta, SKU compatibility map
Telemetry: per-decision reasoning tag added to traces and Console dashboards for cost attribution
tradeoffs: Complexity vs predictability: introducing hedging and probabilistic routing increases controller complexity but reduces sudden spend spikes
Latency vs cost: degrading to quantized models or lower-class SKUs reduces cost but may increase latency and affect quality; staged ladder minimizes user-visible regressions
Operational surface: more knobs (headroom, hedging threshold, ladder order) require sane defaults and guardrails to avoid misconfiguration
implementation_plan: Phase 1: infra - SKU tagging, accelerator_fingerprint metadata, expose spot eviction metric streams (2 sprints)
Phase 2: controller - implement sliding window spend governor and soft-cap throttle with canary lambda (3 sprints)
Phase 3: ladder - model variant registry, compatibility matrix, and fallback actions (2 sprints)
Phase 4: observability - dashboard, per-request decision tag, and cost impact analytics (1 sprint)
Phase 5: rollout - staged rollout to low-traffic tenants, ramp to production with automated rollback hooks (2 weeks)
Expected total: ~8 sprints, cross-team (runtime, allocator, console, evals)
metrics: Primary: tenant spend delta vs baseline (30d), percent of requests served on preferred SKU, SLO breach rate post-rollout
Secondary: avg latency change by ladder step, model quality regressions on eval prompts, spot-eviction mitigation rate
tests_and_eval: Sim test harness that replays production request traces with configurable market price traces and eviction events
A/B: compare current router vs spend-curtain arbiter for a subset of tenants, measure cost and SLOs over 14 days
Quality gate: run representative eval suites after each ladder step to ensure regressions are within acceptable thresholds
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for <5 tenants with synthetic load for 72h
Stage: enable for 10% of traffic across 3 regions, monitor cost and SLOs for 7d
Ramp: increase to 50% over 2 weeks with automated rollback on threshold breaches
Full: flip default once 30d metrics are green
